The facts in brief are as follows :-
 The claimants are the wife, daughter and sons of the deceased  Chandrappa.

On 20.01.2014 at about 14.30 hours, when the deceased was  travelling in the Tata motor L.M.V bearing Reg.No.TN-34/J.2549 along wit  others in shoolagiri to Kalingavaram road, the driver of the 407 bearing  Regn.No.TN-41/1949 belonging to the 1st respondent and insured with the   respondent drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and without  sounding horn and without minding the rules of the road came from opposi  side towards shoolagiri side and caused the accident.
Due to which, the  deceased and some other person sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately   the accident, the deceased was taken to Government Hospital, Krishnagiri https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  Page No.3 of 10  C.M.A  admitted as inpatient in the said hospital.
After taking first-aid treat  was taken to the Fortis Hospital, Bangalore and he was admitted as inpat  from 21.01.2014 to 16.02.2014 and thereafter, he died on 12.05.2016.
Hen  the claimants have filed a claim petition claiming a sum of Rs.35,00,000  the death of the deceased.
4. Before the Tribunal, the claimants have examined three witn  P.W.1 to P.W.3 and marked 22 documents viz., Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.22.
On the s  of the Insurance Company, they have examined two witnesses viz., R.W.1 a  R.W.2 and marked 3 documents viz., Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.

After adjudication,
 Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.12,39,674/-by ordering pay and recovering.
Aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has filed the appeal and th  claimants have filed the cross objection.

The learned counsel appearing for appellant/insurance compa  submitted that, in order to prove that the death of the deceased was due  injuries sustained by the deceased in the accident, no document was mark  before the Tribunal except the discharge summaries issued by the G.H.
 Krishnagiri and Fortis Hospital, Bangalore and the same was marked as Ex  to Ex.P.4.

He further submitted that, the discharge summaries makes it c https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  Page No.4 of 10  C.M.A  that the deceased sustained multiple injuries and after taking treatment  discharged from hospital on 16.02.2014 and no document is available to p  that the deceased had taken treatment in any other hospital.
In the abse  any proof with regard to the fact that the deceased had died due to acci  injuries, the Tribunal awarded compensation by applying multiplier metho  wholly unsustainable.
Accordingly, he prays for allowing the appeal and  dismissal of the cross objection.

6. The learned counsel appearing for the cross objectors submi  by considering all the materials, the Tribunal has rightly arrived at a   that the deceased had died due to the accidental injuries and awarded  compensation by adopting multiplier method, which is wholly sustainable.
Accordingly, he prays for allowing the cross objection and dismissal of   appeal.

Now, the only issue which arises for consideration is wheth  of the deceased in the year 2016 is due to the accident or not.
In order  ascertain the nature of injuries sustained by the deceased, Ex.P.2 to Ex  marked, which reveals that the deceased sustained multiple injuries and   no fracture injury.

Ex.P.3/discharge summary issued by Fortis Hospital, 
 that the final diagnosis was C3-C5 Ossified posterior Longitudinal Ligam  with Cord compression, Hypertension, Diabetes Mellitus, Urethral Stenosi  he discharged from hospital on 16.02.2014.

However, after 16.02.2014, th  claimants have not produced any materials before the Tribunal for taking  further treatment in any other hospital from the date of accident till t  death of the deceased and no post-mortem report or death summary was  marked before the Tribunal.

However, in the absence of any oral and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  Page No.6 of 10  C.
 documentary evidence
